item.title: [ 52] Genshin Impact (nostalgia thread)
item.description:
Genshin Impact launch / 1.0 was probably the most fun /v/ was in years

It launched in like 2020, the whole Hoyo/Gacha thing was new. A full blown AAA budget gacha game was unheard of

It baited a fuckload of anons into it, but at the same time the sense of discovery was really cool

People set up maps n shit for all the landmarks and hidden quests, you had a really big sense of community, people just helped each other

Obviously the BotW shitposting was hilarious and none of us really new how big Genshin really was during that time, and boy did it really blow up

The characters were cute and memorable, chinese made games weren't really big (at least mainstream big) until hoyo slapped their big chink dick on the table

item.title: [ 32] Why is there no "ThinkPad" of printers?
item.description:
It’s 2026. We have reusable rockets and powerful AI, yet consumer printers are still brittle, unreliable nightmares.
Why hasn't any manufacturer built a printer with the ThinkPad philosophy?
Here is what we are missing
>Tank-like build quality, Rugged, durable parts instead of cheap, flimsy plastic that breaks during a routine paper jam.
>True repairability, Modular components (rollers, printheads) that you can swap yourself in five minutes using standard screws and official service manuals.
>Bloatware-free software, No 500MB driver packages, no mandatory cloud accounts, and no forced firmware updates. Just pure, timeless network standards.
>Zero DRM, A machine that accepts toner or ink without demanding a microchip subscription or blocking third-party refills.The legendary HP LaserJet 4000 from the late 90s was the closest we ever got, but the industry completely abandoned that path for the predatory "razor-and-blades" business model.Is the market for a reliable, long-lasting print tool really too small, or is planned obsolescence just too profitable to fight?
What modern machine comes closest to this ideal for you?

item.title: [ 61] Trump's two week war drives diesel prices to all time high
item.description:
https://www.politico.com/news/2026/09/03/diesel-prices-hit-all-time-high-as-trump-administration-brandishes-energy-policies-01063862

U.S. diesel fuel prices hit a record high Thursday afternoon, according to a fuel price monitoring service, surpassing the previous peak set in 2022 as surging crude oil and refining bottlenecks sent the cost of the fuel that underpins a wide swathe of the U.S. economy soaring.

Diesel prices have risen nearly 60 percent in the past 12 months as the U.S. war against Iran has scrambled oil shipments from the Middle East and Russia’s output of the fuel has dwindled because of its war against Ukraine. The new record is likely to spread through the economy and feed inflation that could damage Republican prospects of keeping control of Congress in November’s midterm elections.

Diesel now costs an average of $5.82 a gallon, according to the pricing service GasBuddy, breaking the previous record high of $5.81 set under former President Joe Biden in June 2022 when fuel costs skyrocketed amid Russia’s invasion of Ukraine and the post-Covid global economy.

Vice President JD Vance told reporters at the White House on Thursday that gas prices are high because the Iranian regime is targeting oil tankers moving through the Strait of Hormuz. He also claimed that gas prices “could have been much much higher were it not for our efforts” and downplayed the notion that the world is currently experiencing an energy crisis.

“I can’t repeat this enough, but for the leadership of President Trump and the hard work of our troops, we would have had an energy crisis because the Iranians refused to stop acting like terrorists in the Strait of Hormuz,” Vance said.

item.title: [ 69] New BIS report drops XRPL and Chainlink
item.description:
The BIS just published a pretty interesting paper on putting official government data on a blockchain.

Basically, they take things like GDP and inflation data, create cryptographic fingerprints of the data, combine them into a Merkle tree, and then record the final proof on the XRP Ledger.

That gives you a permanent, timestamped way to verify:

“Did this data actually come from the official source, and has anyone changed it?”

They also use Verifiable Credentials to tie the data back to the official publisher. The proof of concept was extremely fast too, roughly 3–5 seconds to publish and 1–2 seconds to verify.They chose XRPL for the prototype because of its fast finality and low fees. BUT here’s the part XRP maxis seem to be missing:

The BIS explicitly says the system is blockchain-agnostic. XRPL is the blockchain they used for the experiment. It doesn't mean XRPL is the required blockchain.

And the paper actually discusses the 2025 US Department of Commerce + Chainlink work, where Chainlink was used to bring GDP, PCE and other official economic data on-chain.

Basically there are two different layers:

BIS/XRPL:
Government data cryptographic proof blockchain verify authenticity

Chainlink:
Official data Chainlink infrastructure reliably deliver it to blockchains/apps

So no, this paper doesn't prove that XRPL replaces Chainlink. If anything, it shows why these systems can be complementary. The bigger takeaway is that blockchain is becoming a verification/trust layer for official data. XRPL was simply the blockchain used in this particular BIS prototype.

https://www.bis.org/publications/working-paper-1374-verifiable-official-statistics-blockchain-based-approach.pdf

item.description:
>For example, the way the system is designed, if even one barcode on one ballot in a bulk mailing of 10,000 ballots failed to properly scan during the verification process, the entire batch is rejected and sent back to the state, effectively stopping the ballots from being mailed to voters and depriving them of their vote.

https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/elections/whistleblower-usps-systems-mail-ballots-flawed-rcna595361

An anonymous federal official warned in a whistleblower complaint this week that the technical system the U.S. Postal Service built for mail voting is flawed, untested and likely to cause major disruptions in this fall’s midterm elections if it is implemented.

President Donald Trump signed an executive order in March that directed his administration to create federal lists of citizens and asked the Postal Service to transmit mail ballots to only those people. A federal judge has blocked the order from going into effect amid ongoing litigation over its constitutionality; the whistleblower complaint highlights potential issues that could arise if the courts ultimately declare it lawful.

The USPS typically is responsible only for transporting mail ballots between election officials and voters, and the federal government has never kept a central list of all American citizens. Trump ordered the agency to take on an unprecedented and complex role in the process this year amid a broader attempt to exert greater control over the country’s elections and his continued unfounded claims of widespread voter fraud.

The technical system the USPS assembled to vet voters was developed in a “rushed, chaotic, and fundamentally flawed process,” according to a whistleblower complaint sent to the office of Sen. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn., a member of the Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee. Blumenthal sent the complaint to Postmaster General David Steiner on Monday asking for more information.

General Motors plans to assemble a heavy-duty pickup at an Ontario plant as part of a tentative deal with a key union that would pump C$1.1 billion ($791.31 million) into Canada's auto sector as it reels from U.S. tariffs, a union bargaining report said on Saturday.

The investment comes as Canada's auto sector grapples with 25% U.S. tariffs on vehicles, with President Donald Trump pledging to double them to 50% on January 1, 2027. The fate of Canadian auto plants has emerged as a central issue in stalled U.S.-Canada trade negotiations.

The deal is contingent on approval from workers who are voting on Saturday and Sunday. Both Unifor and GM's Canadian division declined comment during the vote.

The C$1.1 billion investment includes a C$691 million commitment to support production of new V8 engines in Ontario that was previously announced in April, the report said.

U.S. President Donald Trump, who has clashed with Ontario Premier Doug Ford in recent days, has also said he will increase tariffs on all Canadian cars and trucks, automotive parts and steel to 50% starting January 1, 2027.

https://www.foxnews.com/politics/appeals-court-delivers-unsettling-ruling-supreme-court-left-no-choice

>A federal appeals court says decades-old Supreme Court precedent forced it to protect the in-home possession of AI-generated child sexual abuse material, as judges warned that rapidly advancing technology has complicated legal lines drawn nearly 25 years ago.

>The ruling exposes a widening gap between Supreme Court precedent and rapidly advancing artificial intelligence. The Seventh Circuit said it was bound by a 2002 Supreme Court decision that rejected restrictions on sexually explicit depictions of fictional children when no actual child was involved in their creation. But two judges warned that modern AI can now generate images virtually indistinguishable from material depicting the abuse of real children.

>"Indeed, in Free Speech Coalition, the Supreme Court addressed the scope of First Amendment protections for virtual CSAM, but that was nearly twenty-five years ago, and the image-generation technology available today was likely unimaginable back then," Judge John Lee wrote. "Given the relentless advancement in artificial intelligence models, we have some concerns about the lines these cases draw, but we are not free to redraw them ourselves."

>The Seventh Circuit affirmed a lower court’s dismissal of one of four charges against Steven Anderegg, who investigators said had hundreds of AI-generated sexually explicit images depicting children on devices seized from his Wisconsin home.

>Anderegg was charged with producing and distributing the AI-generated material, transferring it to a minor under 16, and possessing it. A federal district court dismissed only the possession charge on First Amendment grounds, leaving the other three charges intact.

item.title: [ 92] intense hangover cure research
item.description:
What is your personal go-to cure for a severe hangover? By severe I mean that if you have the energy to cook properly, then you're pretty much a southern belle having "da vapours" and are not actually hungover. An exception will be made if it's a meal that you've cooked so many times that you can make while sleepwalking (e.g. English breakfast, bacon eggs, etc). Please explain your reasoning so that we all may learn from each other and enjoy less sever hangovers. No illegal drugs because that's just cheating. God bless.

My settings:

Drink:
Blue flavoured Powerade
Reasoning:
Electrolytes or some shit but I think mainly because it tastes like the blue Slush Puppies I had as a kid. Nostalgia bonus.

Food:
KFC Zinger Tower Burger (optional extra: 3 hot wings depending on hunger levels)
Reasoning:
Convenient and cheap enough so that your inner Jew doesn't berate you. "Fresh" enough by fast food standards. Good balance of protein and mixed carbs (chicken + potato patty + buns). Is spicy enough on a wypipo level to enliven you without being too caliente to send you stumbling to the WC. South Asians working there can be as automatic and less-than-human as you choose them to be.

Alternate food:
Brazilian coxinhas
Reasoning:
Pretty much same as above, with the added bonus of a bubbly buxom Brazilian babe to brighten up your day. Main negative is that the place closes early, and sometimes the bubbly wholesomeness feels like a judgement on the partying you did before.

item.title: [257] /out/ings with a pipe
item.description:
Last thread >>2856593

This is a thread for enjoying a pipe while doing outdoor activities. If you ask why this belongs on /out/, you've never spent
an evening by the campfire with a pipe silently enjoying the nature around you, and you're missing out.

>how to get started
Purchase a corn cob pipe (or a cheap briar pipe) and a pouch of Half and Half or Captain Black tobacco from a smoke shop
or online. You will need a lighter or match, and something to tamp it with--a large nail works well if you don't have a pipe tool.
Fill the pipe with tobacco, pack it down halfway, top it off, pack it down to 3/4, top it off again, pack gently and enjoy. Smoke
slower than you think you need to, the tobacco tastes best when it is burning cool. Tamp and re-light as needed. If you still
have trouble, try different methods on YouTube until you find one that works for you.
>smoking a pipe will give you cancer
Originally the Surgeon General found that pipe and cigar smokers, following a careful study of the statistics (at a time when
most adults smoked, so they had a good sample size), had insignificant death rate increases. Nowadays, tobacco is being
legislated against while hard drugs are being legalized. Put two and two together. Tobacco is just another good thing under attack by the government.

>muh weed
Not the time or place. Start your own thread.

All tobacco users welcome.
